definition.description: From a declared ready stance in a clear three-path grid, the athlete watches a designated partner. After a randomized wait, the partner points once to the pre-mapped left, right, or forward target. The athlete identifies the true point without guessing, accelerates through the selected target, decelerates on that target's planned exit path, and fully resets. One accepted trial requires an unambiguous cue, correct direction, safe acceleration and braking, and no anticipation. This excludes a simple one-cue forward sprint, pre-planned cut, jump-to-sprint, hip-turn-only drill, assessment, or game simulation.

environment.surface: dry level non-slip direction grid with three clear target paths and exits
environment.space: one protected left/right/forward choice grid with no cross traffic
inspection: target distances, exits, lane separation, surface and footwear
environment.changeRule: Changing cue source, choice count, direction mapping, start, distance, turn, target, exit, surface, recovery, or intent requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: mapping and hold rehearsed at low speed
can accelerate, brake, and reorient safely in every selected path
clear communication with the partner and safe grid exits
session impact, technical-fatigue, and supervision budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: pain, instability, unsafe grid, ambiguous cue, poor visibility, lane conflict, or communication concern
new neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal target distance, wait interval, trial cap, recovery, outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 938 with a focused live visual three-choice sprint research packet.

anatomy.laterality: balanced left, right, and forward choice distribution
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes the movement task and plausible loading sites only; it makes no diagnostic, treatment, injury-prevention, or guaranteed transfer claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate perception-to-action sprint work when the exact cue, grid, exits, and recovery fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Wait for the true point, choose the mapped path, accelerate through it, then own the exit.
secondaryCues: do not guess before the point
use the target path instead of crossing lanes
brake only in the assigned exit
reset fully before the next cue
expectedSensations: brief visual decision followed by whole-body acceleration and controlled braking
unexpectedSensations: pain, instability, dizziness, cue confusion, slip, stumble, or unsafe exit
selfChecks: the cue was visible and unambiguous
the chosen direction matched the point
the target and exit were controlled

observationChecklist: braking, exit, lane safety, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.guessing: lengthen the wait, simplify to one choice, slow the trial, or stop
faultCorrections.ambiguous_cue: reset partner position and mapping before another trial
faultCorrections.crossed_first_step: reduce speed and rehearse each path before returning to random choice
faultCorrections.unsafe_braking: shorten target distance, enlarge the exit, or do not use the task

doNotUseWhen: a simple auditory/visual forward sprint, pre-planned cut, jump sequence, assessment, or game simulation is intended
cue visibility, path spacing, exits, readiness, or supervision is inadequate

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved cue ambiguity, safety, symptom, grid, or quality issues.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to cue, choice count, direction, target, exit, dose, or substitute reruns selection, fatigue, impact, logistics, duration, and validation.

sourceVariant.displayName: Partner Point Reactive Sprint Legacy Skeleton — Source 938

snapshot.description: React to a partner point left, right, or forward.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate live three-choice perception-to-action acceleration with accuracy before speed.

dosage.targetDistance: 3-10 metres or yards declared before the set
dosage.countRule: count only an unambiguous cue, correct direction, safe target pass, assigned exit, and full reset

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The partner waits and points clearly once; the athlete does not anticipate, selects the correct path, accelerates and brakes safely, exits the assigned lane, and direction balance is retained.
stopRules: stop for pain, instability, slip, stumble, wrong lane, unsafe exit, or participant request
stop when cue ambiguity, anticipation, decision error, braking quality, or path safety cannot be restored
stop when fatigue makes the work guessing or conditioning rather than accurate reaction
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Set the partner, mapping, target distances, exits, and randomized wait; observe cue integrity, choices, paths, braking, and recovery; record accepted trials separately from anticipations/errors.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Hold your ready stance, watch the partner, wait for one true point, take the mapped path, accelerate through the target, use the assigned exit, and reset.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate practice of a defined live visual choice-reaction and directional acceleration task; no sport-performance result is guaranteed.

doseScaling.reduce: use one or two choices, shorter targets, lower intent, longer rest, or a separately reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add a jump, turn, contact, extra choices, reduced visibility, speed, distance, or fatigue density automatically.

supportPrompts.athlete: Wait, see the point, choose the mapped path, own the exit, and reset.
supportPrompts.coach: Protect cue integrity and exits; accuracy is separate from movement speed.

legacy.description: Live partner point chooses a left, right, or forward sprint response.
legacy.tempo: randomized hold; one cue; one response; full reset
legacy.loadNote: Bodyweight live visual choice reaction with directional acceleration/braking.
legacy.cardSummary: Candidate three-choice partner-point reactive sprint start.
legacy.coachLanguage: Set cue, grid, paths and exits; separate accepted reactions from guesses.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Wait for the point, take the mapped path, use the exit, and reset.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact cue, grid, direction, braking, surface, exit, communication, and recovery context—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: confirm clear targets/exits and partner visibility
confirm safe acceleration/braking and stop signal
stopSigns: pain, instability, slip, stumble, ambiguous cue, wrong lane, unsafe braking/exit, or stop request
repeated anticipation or decision error after reset
contraindications: symptom, grid, visibility, communication, supervision, or exit conflict
jump, contact, sport simulation, assessment, or different cue-response task
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after revalidation.
Do not automatically substitute a simple auditory start, light cue, pre-planned cut, or reactive test.

score.reviewNotes: Candidate task-only reassessment from live visual choice-reaction evidence; independent calibration remains required.
